**Synopsis:**
European equities fell on a global bond selloff, with euro zone yields hitting multi-year highs. August euro zone inflation rising above 3% (energy-driven) reinforced ECB rate hike expectations for the following week. Euro zone manufacturing surprised to the upside. Stock-specific moves were driven by Novartis (positive trial data), Reckitt (litigation win), and Partners Group (CEO departure, profit warning). The article references hawkish commentary from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh as a contributing global driver of rate hike pricing.
